daily_brief: The collapse of COP31 climate talks in Antalya dominated headlines Monday, with the EU and Pacific island nations rejecting a final text that omitted any reference to fossil fuels [BBC], [The Economist], [Globe and Mail]. UN Secretary-General António Guterres blamed 'powerful fossil fuel interests' for the failure, the worst breakdown since Copenhagen in 2009. Meanwhile, Ukraine expanded its long-range strike capabilities dramatically, sinking the Russian corvette Merkury in Libya's Benghazi port using naval drones deployed 2,400km from the front line [The Guardian], [Al Jazeera]. The Kremlin warned of 'painful consequences' as both Libyan governments condemned the strikes. In a remarkable corporate reversal, Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO just days after the board ruled out his return, with President Trump claiming he personally intervened with the company [France 24], [Financial Times]. Democratic Senator Chuck Schumer vowed investigations into potential wrongdoing. Across Europe, Belgium ground to a halt as a national strike against austerity measures cancelled over 400 flights and shut down public transport [BBC], affecting more than 50,000 passengers as coalition budget negotiations continue.

top_stories.headline: COP31 Climate Talks Collapse as EU Rejects Fossil Fuel-Free Final Text
bullets: UN climate conference in Antalya, Turkey ended Sunday without agreement after becoming the longest COP in history, extending two days past deadline
Final draft text contained no mention of fossil fuels or transition away from them, prompting formal objections from EU, Pacific island nations, and Panama
UN Secretary-General António Guterres blamed 'powerful fossil fuel interests' for blocking progress, comparing tactics to 'Big Tobacco's playbook'
First major COP failure since Copenhagen in 2009; Australian PM Albanese attributed collapse to 'difficult geopolitical times'

top_stories.headline: Ukraine Sinks Russian Warship in Libya Using Long-Range Naval Drones
bullets: Ukrainian forces deployed seven domestically-made naval drones to sink the corvette Merkury at Benghazi naval base, 2,400km from Ukraine's front line
A second Russian cargo ship, MV Angara, was also struck; Ukraine claims it was transporting weapons
Both Libyan governments condemned the attack; Kremlin warned of 'escalation of tensions' and 'painful consequences'
Operation marks significant expansion of Ukraine's long-range strike capability beyond the Black Sea

top_stories.headline: Nvidia Reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO After Trump Claims Direct Intervention
bullets: Nvidia board unanimously voted to reinstate co-founder Jensen Huang as CEO, effective immediately, reversing position from days earlier
Trump told CNBC he directly intervened with Nvidia's board to bring Huang back after his resignation amid affair revelations including alleged Chinese spy
Democratic Senate leader Chuck Schumer vowed full investigation into potential wrongdoing, accusing Trump of prioritizing financial interests over national security
Nvidia shares surged approximately 30-33%, driving Nasdaq up 7% and S&P up 4.3%

top_stories.headline: Belgium Paralyzed by National Strike Against Austerity Measures
bullets: All flights cancelled at Brussels and Charleroi airports between 07:00-21:00 local time, affecting 404 flights and over 50,000 passengers
Underground services halted in Brussels as large protests took place against planned budget cuts
Strike comes as PM Bart De Wever continues coalition talks over budget to cut borrowing costs after King Philippe declined his resignation
Air traffic controllers and public transport workers joined broader cost-of-living protests

top_stories.headline: Russian Strikes Kill 11 in Kyiv Region; 7-Year-Old Rescued After 14 Hours
bullets: Overnight Russian strikes on Dymer village killed 11 people; a 7-year-old boy was rescued alive after 14 hours buried in rubble
A 79-year-old woman was also rescued alive from collapsed residential building and hospitalized
Separate strike on Vyshneve hit grocery store, killing 3 and wounding 13
Over 130 emergency personnel deployed to search sites; Zelensky sent condolences to families
